html:
SMTO-ART-0016 — Artifact unavailable

GUID: a2ce55cd-8ee1-4001-a8de-bf484652bb21
Slug: artifact-unavailable
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't find this saved file for this conversation. The link may be old, the file may not be collected yet, or SMTO couldn't reach it right now.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Artifacts from this run again so SMTO loads the current list, then select the file from that list. A link from an older message may point to a file that no longer exists in this conversation.
  2. If Download all or the conversation Export failed because some files are unavailable, select Download for each file that is still listed. SMTO won't build a ZIP file with missing files, but each available file can still be downloaded.
  3. If the list shows files still waiting, wait for the Task's commands to finish, then select Retry collection. Files are only added after the commands that write them have finished.
  4. If collection keeps failing, open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for the Gateway the Task used. SMTO collects files through the Gateway, the helper program that runs commands on a computer, so it must be online.

What success looks like

  • The file appears in Artifacts from this run and opens or downloads.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete SMTO's data folder or the Task's history to clear the error; the file may still be stored.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected artifact could not be obtained: its ID is malformed or unknown, its status is not available, a temp source is missing on the Gateway, or a collection, export or reconcile request could not complete.

What this means

  • Artifact lookup rejects malformed/missing identity, staging cannot find its file, status is unavailable or a collection/export/reconcile wrapper cannot obtain the selected artifact. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Artifact lookup rejects malformed/missing identity, staging cannot find its file, status is unavailable or a collection/export/reconcile wrapper cannot obtain the selected artifact.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the original ID, scope and registry status with the underlying safe diagnostic.

How to fix it

  • Look up the artifact ID in registered_artifacts and its run's artifact_workspaces row; for ZIP or conversation exports check export_info for unavailable latest versions, and for reconcile failures check Gateway reachability and the Server log. Fix the underlying storage or Gateway problem and refresh the run's artifact list rather than editing registry state.
  • Refresh the owning artifact list and inspect its storage and Gateway availability.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended retained artifact is located or its specific absence/access condition is established.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
